title: Services, transactions, locks, and callbacks

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A transaction creates a reservation, calls stock.save (which returns false), then returns success. Repair the partial-success path.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: An after_commit callback enqueues a job, but the process dies just before enqueue. How can the system find the missing work?

trace.title: Use-case service
trace.detail: Use a service object to name one business action, such as ReserveStock. Use a transaction when its database changes must commit together. A service object by itself supplies no transaction, retry, or permission guarantee.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
A enters the transaction and locks the stock row. B waits for that row. A checks and writes, then commits. B continues and sees the new quantity before deciding. Test with independent connections so the overlap is real.

Callbacks are hidden control flow. A concern can install one when included. Draw callback order and side effects before moving them. A clear use-case method often makes orchestration easier to test.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: Catching an exception inside the transaction and continuing may commit earlier work. Nested transactions are not necessarily independent commits. Read savepoint behavior before promising that an inner rollback undoes everything.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Trace a Rails transaction and explain what after_commit does and does not promise. Give a concrete failure example.
